ovarian-torsion.core: Abrupt unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting suggests twisting of the adnexal vascular pedicle, requiring rapid ovarian-preserving surgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovarian cyst/mass, especially >5 cm; pregnancy, ovulation induction, prior torsion
Functional cysts and mature teratomas common lead points; adolescents may torsion a normal ovary

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent severe pain from twisting/untwisting; adnexal tenderness or mass; mild leukocytosis possible
Fever, guarding, peritoneal findings may indicate advanced ischemia; absence does not reassure
Pregnancy test can be positive with torsion; pregnancy does not establish ectopic implantation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Venous/lymphatic outflow obstruction → congestion and edema, followed by reduced arterial inflow
Dual arterial supply may preserve detectable flow despite clinically important vascular compromise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; assess shock, competing surgical diagnoses
★ **Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler** first; transvaginal when feasible, transabdominal in younger adolescents
Enlarged edematous ovary, peripheral follicles, free fluid, twisted pedicle support diagnosis
★ **Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion**; no laboratory test reliably rules it out
High clinical suspicion → diagnostic laparoscopy; no serial imaging delay to prove loss of flow

rows.label: Tx
items: NPO, IV access, fluids for dehydration, analgesia/antiemetic; urgent gynecology consultation
★ **Laparoscopic detorsion with ovarian preservation**, even if dark/blue appearance
Cystectomy if safely feasible; friable edematous ovary → defer cyst removal and reassess
Oophorectomy only if unavoidable tissue destruction or compelling malignancy concern; avoid removal for color alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Ovarian infarction, diminished ovarian reserve, infertility, recurrent torsion
Unnecessary extensive resection sacrifices viable ovarian tissue; timely treatment maximizes salvage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Residual cyst → **ultrasound at 6–12 weeks**; persistent significant cyst may need elective cystectomy
Ovulation suppression may reduce recurrent functional cysts; oophoropexy individualized after recurrent torsion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine gestation or concerning pregnancy-location evaluation
Ruptured hemorrhagic cyst: abrupt pain with free fluid; often improves without persistent torsion signs
PID: discharge, cervical motion tenderness, STI risk; bilateral symptoms more typical

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea permissible despite risks; reassess sedation/respiration
Codeine fails → morphine/oxycodone; pain mimics depression; wears off early → shorten interval

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids**, short-acting for breakthrough; constipation → keep dose, add stimulant laxative

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals
Advanced dementia refusing intake → comfort hand-feeding by mouth; no tubes or IV

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Hospice: unrelated conditions remain treatable; no DNR requirement; enrollment revocable if goals change
Cancer pain: escalating requests → tolerance/progression, not addiction; past OUD never limits analgesia

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

table.title: Care settings
rows: Adjust with hospice team; avoid readmission

pelvic-organ-prolapse.name: Pelvic organ prolapse
pelvic-organ-prolapse.scope: Anterior compartment (cystocele), posterior compartment (rectocele, enterocele), apical compartment (uterine prolapse, vaginal vault prolapse, procidentia), pelvic floor muscle training, pessary, surgical repair
pelvic-organ-prolapse.core: Loss of pelvic support causes a vaginal bulge with pressure, urinary symptoms, or obstructed defecation, often worse when standing or straining.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vaginal births, increasing age, menopause, obesity, connective-tissue weakness
Chronic cough/constipation, heavy lifting; hysterectomy predisposes to vaginal vault descent

rows.label: Clues
items: Visible/palpable protrusion, incomplete bladder emptying, stress leakage, need to splint vagina for defecation
★ **Urinary retention or hydronephrosis** with advanced descent → evaluate obstruction promptly
Symptoms improve supine; mucosal rubbing can produce spotting or ulceration

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Levator ani injury and fascial/ligamentous failure permit descent of one or several vaginal compartments

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pelvic examination during Valsalva**, sometimes standing; isolate compartments with speculum
POP-Q stages descent relative to hymen; measure postvoid residual when voiding symptoms present
Urinalysis for urinary symptoms; creatinine/renal ultrasound when severe obstruction suspected
Reduce prolapse during cough stress testing to unmask occult stress incontinence before surgery

rows.label: Tx
items: Asymptomatic prolapse → observation; bothersome mild disease → pelvic floor muscle training
★ **Vaginal pessary** for conservative treatment, frail/high surgical risk; fit, teach removal, schedule mucosal checks
Vaginal estrogen for atrophic mucosa when suitable; does not restore structural support
★ Persistent symptoms → compartment repair plus **apical suspension** when support deficient
No future vaginal intercourse desired → colpocleisis; preservation/reconstruction chosen according to goals

rows.label: Complications
items: Ulceration, recurrent UTI, retention, obstructive kidney injury; recurrence after repair
Neglected pessary → erosion/fistula; surgery → dyspareunia, new urinary leakage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight reduction, treat constipation/cough, reduce straining; pelvic floor exercises and pessary follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Urethral diverticulum: focal anterior mass, postvoid dribbling, recurrent infection
Vaginal cyst: discrete lesion without generalized descent during strain

table.title: Compartments
rows: Small bowel → upper posterior vagina/vault; peristalsis
Entire uterus prolapses beyond vaginal introitus

pelvic-organ-prolapse.evidence: Not checked online; established urogynecology evaluation and conservative/surgical management.

placenta-accreta-spectrum.name: Placenta accreta spectrum
placenta-accreta-spectrum.scope: Placenta accreta, placenta increta, placenta percreta, prior cesarean and placenta previa risk, antenatal ultrasound diagnosis, scheduled cesarean hysterectomy
placenta-accreta-spectrum.core: Abnormal placental invasion into myometrium after prior uterine surgery, causing catastrophic postpartum hemorrhage if manual removal is attempted.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Prior cesarean delivery + placenta previa** (strongest risk; rises with each cesarean)
Prior myomectomy, dilation and curettage, Asherman syndrome, advanced maternal age

rows.label: Clues
items: Often **asymptomatic** until delivery; painless third-trimester bleeding if previa coexists
★ **Placenta fails to detach** after delivery with brisk bleeding on traction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective **decidua basalis** at scar site lets chorionic villi attach directly to myometrium

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Antenatal ultrasound with Doppler**: placental lacunae, lost retroplacental clear zone
**Pelvic MRI** when ultrasound is inconclusive or posterior/percreta invasion is suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Scheduled cesarean hysterectomy at 34–35+6 wk** at tertiary center; **leave placenta in situ**
★ **Never attempt manual placental removal** → triggers massive hemorrhage
Massive transfusion protocol ready; antenatal betamethasone if delivering <37 wk
IF found unexpectedly during delivery → stop traction, close hysterotomy, perform hysterectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: **Massive postpartum hemorrhage**, DIC, hysterectomy/infertility, bladder or ureteral injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary primary cesarean deliveries; screen all placenta previa patients with targeted ultrasound

rows.label: Mimics
items: Retained placenta: normal cleavage plane present; detaches with manual extraction
Uterine atony: boggy uterus after complete placental delivery; responds to uterotonics
Placenta previa alone: painless bleeding, but normal retroplacental clear zone on ultrasound

placenta-accreta-spectrum.evidence: Not checked online; established ACOG/SMFM teaching.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.scope: Community-acquired, hospital-acquired, ventilator-associated, aspiration, atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma)
pneumonia.core: Acute lower respiratory infection with a new infiltrate; severity, acquisition setting, and resistance risks determine disposition and empiric antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, COPD, age, immunosuppression
Dysphagia, absent gag/cough (stroke, dementia, Parkinson), impaired consciousness → aspiration
HAP ≥48 hours hospitalized; VAP ≥48 hours after intubation
Prior MRSA/Pseudomonas isolation or recent hospitalization with IV antibiotics → resistant pathogens

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, cough, sputum, focal crackles; older adults: confusion; children: lower-lobe disease may refer abdominal pain
★ Severe: **hypoxemia, hypotension, tachypnea**, multilobar disease; ventilation or pressors → ICU
Legionella: water exposure, diarrhea, hyponatremia; Mycoplasma: school-age/young adult, indolent dry cough, cold agglutinins
Immunocompromised, diffuse bilateral interstitial/alveolar infiltrates, exertional hypoxemia → **Pneumocystis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar inflammation/exudate → shunt and impaired oxygenation
Chemical aspiration pneumonitis: sterile gastric injury; severity tracks **volume and acidity**; rapid improvement possible

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CXR** first; CT if strong suspicion despite nondiagnostic radiograph
**CURB-65** 0–1 or low PSI → outpatient; severe CAP → blood/sputum cultures, Legionella antigen ± PCR
Low procalcitonin alone does not justify withholding initial antibiotics in radiographically confirmed bacterial CAP
Gram-positive lancet diplococci → **S pneumoniae**: commonest CAP; lobar consolidation, high fever, often post-viral URI
Small gram-negative coccobacilli, smoker/COPD → **H influenzae**

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen, fluids for hypoperfusion; drain empyema; narrow antibiotics to cultures
★ Aspiration pneumonia: usual CAP coverage; **add anaerobic coverage only for abscess/empyema**
Anaerobes: **ampicillin-sulbactam**; older exam questions may expect **clindamycin**, even without abscess
Stable nonsevere CAP: ATS 2025 permits 3–4 days; classic ≥5-day rule remains for severe disease
★ Severe noninfluenza CAP → consider **systemic corticosteroids**; nonsevere CAP → avoid routine steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Parapneumonic effusion, empyema, bacteremia, respiratory failure, sepsis
S aureus: postinfluenza necrotizing pneumonia; child failing amoxicillin, dense consolidation/effusion
Aspiration (alcoholism, intubation) → **lung abscess**: dependent-segment cavity, air-fluid level, foul sputum
Antibiotic exposure → C difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, smoking cessation, swallowing evaluation
Aspiration/VAP prevention: head elevation 30–45°, oral care, early liberation from ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: thrombotic risk, pleuritic pain, no infectious source
HF: bilateral edema, elevated JVP, cardiac dysfunction

table.title: Empiric adult regimens
rows: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + azithromycin; doxycycline alternative; or levofloxacin
Antipseudomonal: cefepime, ceftazidime, or piperacillin/tazobactam; usually 7 days

population-health-and-quality-improvemen.name: Population health and quality improvement
population-health-and-quality-improvemen.scope: Program evaluation, outcome and process measures, health equity, PDSA cycles
population-health-and-quality-improvemen.core: Improve care for a defined population through measurable aims, iterative system changes, and attention to unequal access and outcomes.

rows.label: Principle
items: Population denominator includes eligible people missing visits, not only those receiving care
Equity: stratify outcomes by language, race/ethnicity, geography, disability, insurance, deprivation
Greater relative **primary care investment** improves population health, reduces disparities

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Define **measurable aim**, population, baseline, timeframe; engage patients/frontline staff
★ **PDSA**: plan small change → do → study results → act/adapt before scaling
Stratify measures, address interpreter/transport/cost barriers, monitor unintended consequences

rows.label: Don't
items: Do not assume a favorable outcome proves causation without comparison and context
Avoid blaming individuals for failures created by unreliable workflows

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Run/control charts distinguish routine common-cause variation from special-cause signals over time
Program evaluation: reach, fidelity, effectiveness, cost, sustainability versus original goals
Education program → measure knowledge/behavior change; small cohort cannot detect morbidity/mortality

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Process success ≠ patient benefit**; assess both and choose valid denominators
★ **Risk adjustment** improves comparison; also report disparities so adjustment cannot conceal inequity
Before–after improvement may reflect secular trends, case-mix change, regression to mean

population-health-and-quality-improvemen.evidence: Established quality-improvement and program-evaluation principles; no guideline-dependent thresholds.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Jagged/incomplete placenta, vessels to membrane edge (**succenturiate lobe**) → retained tissue; oozing → coagulopathy
Shock exceeding visible loss → concealed hematoma; post-cesarean distention, hematocrit drop → **intra-abdominal hemorrhage**
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis
Vulvar hematoma: **pudendal artery** branch, often operative delivery; vaginal/uterine arteries → deep or retroperitoneal

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding
Inversion: round fleshy introitus mass after cord traction, absent abdominal fundus, shock

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

preterm-labor.name: Preterm labor
preterm-labor.scope: Preterm labor (<37 weeks), cervical insufficiency, tocolysis (indomethacin, nifedipine), antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone), magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, GBS chemoprophylaxis
preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; prior preterm birth + cervix <25 mm before 24 weeks
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate withdrawn 2023; progesterone without short cervix not routinely recommended
Older exam questions may expect 17-hydroxyprogesterone from 16–20 weeks after prior spontaneous preterm birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection
Pregnancy: progesterone ureteral relaxation + uterine compression → **stasis**; physiologic right-sided ureteral dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; pyelonephritis → heavy pyuria, WBC clumps/casts; negative nitrites don't exclude
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics
Febrile non-toilet-trained child → **catheterized** urinalysis/culture; bag/clean-catch contaminate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized
Febrile infant → **cefotaxime/ceftriaxone**; first-generation cefazolin inadequate

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen
Recurrence ≥3/year or ≥2 in 6 months → postcoital or daily nitrofurantoin/TMP-SMX
Sporadic postcoital cystitis → **void before/after intercourse**; stop diaphragm/spermicide; condoms don't prevent

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV fluids + ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

vulvar-cancer.name: Vulvar cancer
vulvar-cancer.scope: Squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma of the vulva, lichen sclerosus malignant transformation, vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), Paget disease of the vulva, staging, wide local excision, sentinel node biopsy
vulvar-cancer.core: Persistent vulvar pruritus with a focal ulcer, plaque, or mass requires biopsy, especially in an older patient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV-related disease: smoking, immunosuppression; HPV-independent disease: older age, lichen sclerosus
Prior vulvar HSIL/VIN; chronic symptoms repeatedly treated without tissue diagnosis delay detection
Prior cervical neoplasia: HPV field risk; new vulvar mass → primary cancer, metastasis rare

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonhealing lesion, bleeding, dyspareunia, focal pain; enlarged inguinal nodes suggest regional spread
★ **Changing pigmented lesion** requires melanoma evaluation; amelanotic lesions also occur

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Squamous carcinoma spreads locally, then to inguinofemoral nodes; nodal involvement strongly influences prognosis
HPV-associated HSIL and HPV-independent differentiated VIN are distinct precursor pathways

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Punch/incisional biopsy** of suspicious lesion; sample viable edge, not only necrotic center
Document lesion size, depth, focality, proximity to midline; examine groin nodes
Suspicious nodes → ultrasound-guided sampling; advanced local extent → pelvic MRI and metastatic imaging
Stage by stromal invasion, adjacent-organ extension, and nodal/distant spread; evaluate multifocal disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive disease → **wide local excision** with negative margins
Microinvasive SCC ≤1 mm stromal invasion generally needs no groin-node surgery
★ Unifocal **<4 cm**, invasion >1 mm, clinically negative nodes → sentinel-node biopsy
Larger/multifocal or node-positive disease → groin treatment; locally advanced → chemoradiation and/or surgery
Paget → excision; VIN → excision, or laser/imiquimod after excluding invasion

rows.label: Complications
items: Local recurrence, nodal metastasis; surgery/radiation → lymphedema, wound breakdown, sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: HPV vaccination, tobacco cessation; high-potency topical corticosteroids for lichen sclerosus, continued surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lichen simplex chronicus: diffuse scratch-induced thickening; biopsy persistent focal changes
Candidiasis: yeast on microscopy, responds to antifungal; persistent lesion still needs sampling

table.title: Histologic clues
rows: Ulcerated/keratotic mass; HPV or inflammatory pathway
Asymmetry, irregular color/border; Breslow depth guides management
Chronic eczematous red plaque; intraepithelial glandular cells

vulvar-cancer.evidence: Excision/node selection checked 2026-10-30: [NCI PDQ](https://www.cancer.gov/types/vulvar/hp/vulvar-treatment-pdq); remaining pathology established teaching.

vulvar-dermatoses.name: Vulvar dermatoses
vulvar-dermatoses.scope: Lichen sclerosus, lichen simplex chronicus, lichen planus, punch biopsy, topical high-potency corticosteroids
vulvar-dermatoses.core: Chronic vulvar itching, pain, or architectural change requires morphologic diagnosis and biopsy of suspicious or treatment-resistant lesions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Lichen sclerosus: prepubertal/postmenopausal peaks, autoimmune associations; can occur at any age
Lichen simplex: eczema, irritants, persistent scratching; lichen planus: mucocutaneous inflammatory disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus or burning, dyspareunia, fissures; examine perianal skin, vagina and oral mucosa
★ **Nonhealing ulcer, focal thickening, bleeding or changing pigment** → exclude malignancy
Severe scarring may narrow introitus or obscure normal structures; vaginal involvement narrows differential

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sclerosus/planus: immune-mediated epithelial injury; simplex: itch-scratch cycle causes lichenification

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Careful vulvar examination; persistent focal white plaque or atypical lesion → **punch biopsy** before steroids
Erosive lesions: sample active edge with intact epithelium; avoid only ulcer center
Wet mount/KOH or yeast testing when infection suspected; repeated empiric antifungals can delay correct diagnosis
Assess architectural changes and symptom response longitudinally; consider oral/dermatology examination with mucosal disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sclerosus → **clobetasol ointment**, initial intensive course followed by individualized maintenance
★ Simplex → eliminate trigger and **break scratching cycle** with topical corticosteroid, emollients, nighttime measures
Planus → high-potency topical corticosteroid; erosive vaginal disease may need specialist intravaginal/systemic treatment
Avoid fragranced soaps/wipes and harsh cleansing; bland petrolatum reduces friction and barrier injury
Persistent lesion despite adherence → reassess diagnosis/biopsy rather than indefinitely escalating steroid blindly

rows.label: Complications
items: Sclerosus: vulvar SCC risk and permanent loss of architecture; adequate treatment reduces risk
Erosive planus: adhesions/stenosis; all forms may impair sexual function and quality of life
Excessive unsupervised steroid use → local atrophy; undertreating confirmed sclerosus also causes tissue damage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Regular **surveillance and self-examination** for new focal lesions; continue maintenance when disease active
Avoid irritants, treat coexisting infection/eczema, reduce friction; discuss lubricants and sexual pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candidiasis: yeast/hyphae or positive culture, discharge; no progressive scarring
Vulvar Paget disease: persistent eczematous plaque despite usual treatment; diagnostic biopsy

table.title: Morphology
rows: Porcelain-white thin plaques; figure-eight, labial resorption
Thick leathery excoriated plaques; accentuated skin markings
Painful glazed red erosions; lacy white borders

vulvar-dermatoses.evidence: Not checked online; established vulvar dermatology and biopsy-directed management.
